note_on_method: Two of the five filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Mount Pleasant. Free does, because the Town writes "Drop-in play is free" under three of its four venues and prices the fourth. Indoor does, because the Town's own page is split under the headings Indoor and Outdoor and three venues sit under the first. Outdoor has two venues (Miriam Brown and the Park West tennis courts) and lights has one, so neither reaches the three a page needs.

slots.why_this_filter:
Three of Mount Pleasant's four venues are free, and the Town says so under each one rather than leaving it to be assumed. Park West Gym: "Drop-in play is free." The Deb Gym at Town Hall: the same sentence. Miriam Brown Community Center: "Drop-in play is free and first come, first served." Park West Tennis Courts: "Drop-in play is first come first served and free."

Eighteen of the town's nineteen courts are on this page: ten at Park West, four at the Deb Gym, four at Miriam Brown. Between them they carry every scheduled session in Mount Pleasant except the Senior Center's afternoons. A parks department that does not charge for a court rarely thinks to write down that it is free, and Mount Pleasant wrote it down four times. It is one of seven cities on this site with a free court.

Free here comes with conditions the Town states in the same paragraph. In the gyms you must sign in, and you play at the session times and not otherwise. Paddles and balls are never provided at a free venue.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the Town of Mount Pleasant states that drop-in play on it costs nothing. Three qualify. Park West qualifies twice over, because the Town prices both of its entries at the same address with the word free: the gym under Indoor and the tennis courts under Outdoor. The Deb Gym at Town Hall qualifies on "Drop-in play is free." Miriam Brown Community Center qualifies on "Drop-in play is free and first come, first served."

The Senior Center is excluded, and deliberately. Its court is "free for members of the Senior Center" and a guest fee for everyone else, "$5 for Mt. Pleasant residents and $10 for those residing outside of Mt. Pleasant", and play is for people 50 and older. Free for a member is not free for the public. That is a closer call than it looks: it is the one Mount Pleasant venue that provides paddles and balls as well as the net, so for a member it is the cheapest court in town.

faqs.a: Yes, in the Town's words under each entry: "Drop-in play is free." This site describes a venue as free only when the operator writes it, and Mount Pleasant does, for three venues and both halves of Park West.
In the gyms it is provided. Outdoors it is lent on weekdays, from the Program Building at Park West or the G.M. Darby Building at Miriam Brown; outside those hours bring your own.
No. Clinics are $50 for residents and $80 for non-residents, and private lessons are priced by the hour. Those are lesson prices; the courts themselves cost nothing.

slots.why_this_filter:
Eleven of Mount Pleasant's nineteen courts are indoors, at three of its four venues, and the Town states it in the plainest way an operator can: its pickleball page is divided under two headings, Indoor and Outdoor, and the Senior Center, Park West Gym and The Deb Gym at Town Hall sit under the first.

Indoor here means a gymnasium floor at a scheduled time. Nets are "provided for players to set up", and players are told to "enter at their designated time and prepare for breakdown a few minutes prior to end time". An indoor court in Mount Pleasant exists for its session and not otherwise.

Between them the three gyms cover every weekday and, in the autumn of 2026, eight Sundays. None of them has an evening. The reason to want this page is a court that does not depend on daylight or weather, and Mount Pleasant has more of them than it has outdoor courts.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the Town lists it under the Indoor heading of its pickleball page with a count. Three qualify.

Park West, on "Park West Gym / 6 Courts", the largest indoor count in the town. The venue also holds four outdoor courts, which make up its ten and do not appear on this page. The Deb Gym at Town Hall, on "The Deb Gym at Town Hall / 4 Courts", qualifying on four through volleyball season because the count is stated and the reduction to two is printed beside it. The Senior Center, on "Mount Pleasant Senior Center 50+ / 1 Court", which carries its own conditions: players 50 and older, free for members, a guest fee for everyone else.

What does not qualify is any court the Town lists under Outdoor: Miriam Brown's four and the Park West tennis courts' four. The Park West four are the town's only lit courts, so evening play in Mount Pleasant is an outdoor matter.

faqs.q: When can I play indoors in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: Park West Gym Tuesdays and Thursdays 8:00 am to noon and listed Sundays; the Deb Gym Mondays 1:00 to 3:00 pm, Wednesdays 9:00 am to noon and Fridays 8:00 am to noon; the Senior Center Tuesday and Thursday 3:00 to 4:50 pm and Friday 3:00 to 5:50 pm.

faqs.q: Is there an evening indoor session?
faqs.a: Not one the Town prints. Every indoor session on its page is a weekday morning or afternoon, or an autumn Sunday morning at Park West Gym. The evening group plays outdoors on the lit Park West tennis courts.

faqs.q: Why are there sometimes only two courts at the Deb Gym?
faqs.a: Volleyball season. From September 18 to October 31 the Town says open gym "will only be played on two pickleball courts"; in the other weeks it is four.
